subject: covr does not evaluate coverage of nimble functions

messages.author: 46f76d1903dc6874
messages.subject: covr does not evaluate coverage of nimble functions
parts:
I'm developing a package that depends on nimble. I have a custom distribution that I register with nimble, so I have a script inside of the R/ folder that just has all of those nimbleFunctions defined. Something about them being nimble functions causes covr to ignore those lines of code (if no R functions are in the script, it ignores the script entirely). This results in those lines not being considered in coverage reports (e.g. generated for covr.io). 

I'm guessing it's much more complicated that it might seem at first glance, but I wanted to flag it here just so devs and others are aware. I did find a hacky workaround that I'll use in the meantime. See the following basic example.

r_function_add <- function(a, b) {
  return(a + b)
}
nimble_function_add <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(a = double(1), b = double(1)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    return(r_function_add(a, b))
  }
)

Then, testthat tests can be run on nimble_function_add() and coverage corresponding to R_function_add() will be reported.

messages.subject: Re: covr does not evaluate coverage of nimble functions
parts:
Thanks Vincent.  It will be interesting to see what you learn.

Having the compilable code in a nimbleFunction method (run) call an R function will work in uncompiled execution but not compiled execution.  I don't know how covr works but it wouldn't surprise me if it doesn't know what to do with a nimbleFunction.

-Perry

Thanks!
